subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Knitting forms fabric by...
questions.explain: Knitting builds fabric from interlocking loops of yarn worked with needles.

questions.q: Red is often chosen in branding to suggest...
questions.explain: Red carries strong associations of energy, excitement and urgency, useful for grabbing attention.

questions.q: The CMYK colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, key/black) is the standard ink set used in colour printing.

questions.q: Increasing the 'contrast' of a photo does what?
options: Makes darks darker and lights lighter
questions.explain: Increasing contrast widens the difference between the lightest and darkest tones.

questions.q: A sculpture designed to be viewed from all sides 'in the round' is...
options: A relief carved into a flat background
questions.explain: Sculpture in the round is freestanding and can be walked around and viewed from every angle.

questions.q: Abstract Expressionism is characterised by...
questions.explain: Abstract Expressionism used large-scale, energetic, often non-figurative gestural marks.

questions.q: When you give your personal 'interpretation' of an artwork, you are explaining...
options: What you think it means or communicates
questions.explain: Interpretation offers your view of the meaning, message or mood the artwork conveys.

questions.q: 'Smocking' is a technique that...
options: Gathers fabric with stitches to create decorative texture and stretch
questions.explain: Smocking gathers and stitches fabric to make a flexible, decoratively textured surface.

questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: Around the edges of the frame
In the exact centre of the image
Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

questions.q: What does the 'white balance' setting on a camera adjust?
options: The colour cast so whites appear neutral under different lighting
questions.explain: White balance corrects colour casts so that whites look neutral under different light sources.

questions.q: In weaving, the threads held under tension on the loom that run lengthways are the...
questions.explain: The warp threads run lengthways and are held taut on the loom while the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: What is 'sgraffito'?
options: Scratching through a top layer to reveal a colour beneath
questions.explain: Sgraffito scratches through a surface layer to expose a contrasting colour or layer underneath.

questions.q: A 'relief' sculpture is one where...
options: Forms project from a flat background
questions.explain: In relief, the design is raised from (or sunk into) a flat background rather than standing free.

questions.q: What is a watercolour 'wash'?
options: Thick paint applied with a knife
A thin, transparent layer of diluted paint
questions.explain: A wash is a thin, transparent layer of watercolour spread over an area to build colour gradually.

questions.q: A slow shutter speed used on moving water typically creates...
questions.explain: A slow shutter speed records movement over time, smoothing flowing water into a soft blur.

questions.q: Which artist created the famous ceiling of the Sistine Chapel during the Renaissance?
questions.explain: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling, a masterpiece of the Italian Renaissance.

questions.q: What is 'impasto' in painting?
options: Painting only in black and white
Paint thinned to a watery wash
Thick paint applied so brush or knife marks stand out
questions.explain: Impasto is thickly applied paint that leaves visible, textured marks on the surface.

questions.q: Batik is a textile technique that uses what to resist dye?
questions.explain: In batik, hot wax is applied to fabric so the waxed areas resist the dye.

questions.q: A 'hue' refers to which property of colour?
options: The pure colour itself, such as red or blue
questions.explain: Hue is the name of the pure colour, such as red, yellow or blue, before tints or shades are added.

questions.q: 'Surface decoration' in textiles refers to...
options: Patterns or marks added onto the surface of a fabric
The fibre the fabric is made from
The way the cloth is woven
questions.explain: Surface decoration covers techniques such as printing, embroidery or dyeing applied to a fabric's surface.

questions.q: What is casting in sculpture?
options: Pouring liquid material into a mould to set into shape
questions.explain: Casting pours a liquid such as molten metal or plaster into a mould, where it hardens into the form.

questions.q: The RGB colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: RGB (red, green, blue) is the additive light model used by screens and digital devices.
